canonical.name: Canonical morphisms between parenthesised tensor words are built from associators, unitors, inverses, tensoring with identities, and composition
The word category W is monoidal under binary concatenation with the empty word as unit
Coherence compares only canonical morphisms between parenthesisations of one ordered list and says nothing about arbitrary parallel maps or reordering
Strictification and coherence let the monoid-object axioms be written without explicit associators
The free-word formulation and the canonical-map formulation of coherence imply one another
Every diagram in a monoidal category need not commute
Strictification gives monoidal equivalence, not isomorphism
A monoidal category need not be equivalent to one that is both skeletal and strict
Coherence does not identify arbitrary parallel morphisms in a monoidal category
Strictification itself does not require the axiom of choice
A five-fold tensor product admits many explicit canonical comparison maps, all equal by coherence
The word category on words of length three makes the free monoidal structure concrete
Strictification can be computed explicitly for a cartesian monoidal category
Formally distinct parenthesised words can evaluate to the same object in a specific monoidal category
A monoid object can be written with or without explicit associators once coherence is available
